title: Essence Drain Contagion Lich Build Guide
summary: A source-linked Chaos DoT guide that separates pack spreading, boss upkeep and Full-Life or Low-Life endgame decisions.
description: Complete guide for a Path of Exile 2 Essence Drain and Contagion Lich build on the 0.5.4 baseline.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: A Lich spreading violet Essence Drain and Contagion through a dark enemy pack

sections.title: Build Overview
paragraphs: ED + Contagion is effective because it turns target selection into propagation: Contagion marks the pack, Essence Drain supplies the damaging debuff, and a death carries the package onward. The build feels poor when those two casts land on unrelated targets, so aiming and pack order matter more than another line of tooltip damage.

For bosses, propagation disappears. The build becomes a maintenance setup: keep Essence Drain active, add Despair only when the target warrants the cast, maintain Dark Effigy totems, and move while damage over time continues. That mobility is the payoff for accepting a slower, layered damage ramp.

This guide separates the three real rhythms — the Mapping clear loop, the Boss Opening sequence and the Sustained Boss loop — so the cast order of Essence Drain, Contagion, Despair and Dark Effigy is never ambiguous.
bullets: Apply the two-skill spread setup to a pack, then move while the damage resolves.
Refresh Essence Drain and the chosen curse before their coverage expires.
Against bosses, add only the auxiliary skills verified for the selected variant; do not merge every guide's buttons.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Low gear floor for campaign progression.
Damage continues while the player repositions.
Contagion can turn one successful application into pack clear.
cons: Damage is delayed rather than immediate.
Bossing needs several debuffs or auxiliary skills.
Different endgame guides disagree on auxiliary skills and defence.

sections.title: Combat Rotations
paragraphs: The build has three different rhythms. Mapping is a spread loop, the boss opening is a fixed setup sequence, and sustained bossing is a repeating maintenance loop. Mixing them up — casting Contagion on a lone boss, or standing still to spam Essence Drain — is the most common mistake.

Mapping Rotation (clear loop): cast Contagion first so the pack is marked contagious, then land Essence Drain on any target inside that area. Because the target is contagious, ED's spread copies the DoT to every nearby Contagion-affected enemy. Move immediately; the damage resolves while you reposition. Dark Effigy can be planted to auto-maintain ED/Despair on the cluster.

Boss Opening Rotation (how the fight starts): open with Despair — the curse that lowers chaos resistance and amplifies everything after it. Then plant Dark Effigy, the totem/support that auto-casts ED + Despair for hands-free uptime. Finally apply Essence Drain to lay the main DoT. Contagion is normally skipped on a single boss because there is nothing to spread to.

Sustained Boss Rotation (the repeating loop once opened): re-apply Essence Drain before its duration expires, keep the Dark Effigy totem alive and repositioned (it can miss a moving boss, so you must re-cast ED yourself), refresh Despair when it falls off, and keep moving between mechanics. The rhythm is refresh → reposition → refresh, never stationary casting.
bullets: Mapping: Contagion → Essence Drain → move (optional Dark Effigy).
Boss open: Despair → Dark Effigy → Essence Drain.
Sustained: refresh Essence Drain → keep Dark Effigy → refresh Despair → move.

steps.label: Campaign start (pre-core)
body: Before ED + Contagion unlock, use a chaos or filler DoT spell and stabilize life, resistances and movement speed. Do not force the DoT chain early.

steps.label: Acts 2–4 (core online)
body: Run Essence Drain + Contagion once available. Add reliable single-target support (Dark Effigy, Despair) without sacrificing the basic spread loop.

steps.label: Campaign end
body: Build Energy Shield and recovery while maintaining gem levels.

steps.label: Early maps
body: Decide whether the default Full-Life shell or a later Low-Life transition is being followed.

skills.role: Primary chaos DoT; the damaging debuff that spreads through Contagion.
whyUse: It is the source of the persistent chaos damage — once applied to a Contagion-affected target it spreads to the whole pack, and on bosses it is the maintained DoT.
whenReplace: Never replaced; it is the core damage skill from leveling to endgame. Only supports and gem levels change.
mappingBossingDiff: Mapping: cast Contagion first, then Essence Drain on a target inside it to trigger the spread, then move. Bossing: maintain Essence Drain uptime as the repeating DoT; the totem can help but on a moving boss you must re-apply it yourself.
notes: Exact support links and gem levels are pending PC verification.

skills.role: Spread enabler; marks enemies as contagious so Essence Drain propagates.
whyUse: It is the prerequisite for pack clear: without Contagion on the targets, Essence Drain does not spread. Cast it before Essence Drain.
whenReplace: Keep in the mapping toolkit. On a single isolated boss it has little use (nothing to spread to); some variants drop it for bosses.
mappingBossingDiff: Mapping: cast first into the pack center to enable spread. Bossing: usually skipped on a lone boss unless adds are present.
notes: Spread condition and range are pending PC verification.

skills.role: Totem/support that auto-casts Essence Drain (and Despair) to maintain the DoT hands-free.
whyUse: It maintains ED/Despair uptime while you reposition, reducing manual refresh burden.
whenReplace: Keep for bossing and dense mapping; on a fast-moving boss you must still manually re-apply ED because the totem may miss.
mappingBossingDiff: Mapping: optional, plant on a cluster. Bossing: plant at fight open, keep it alive and repositioned.
notes: Moving-boss uptime is the known weak point; exact contribution pending PC verification.

skills.role: Curse that lowers the target's chaos resistance, amplifying the DoT.
whyUse: It is the curse that directly raises ED damage on the cursed target; apply it before committing the DoT.
whenReplace: Keep; it is the single-target amplifier, not a damage competitor.
mappingBossingDiff: Mapping: optional on rares that survive. Bossing: apply first at fight open, then maintain uptime.
notes: Curse effect / gem level pending PC verification.

skills.role: Variant-dependent buff area that adds damage or defense.
whyUse: Some variants use it as a damage/defense amplifier; treat it as optional until the chosen guide verifies it.
whenReplace: Variant choice; keep only if your selected planner includes it.
mappingBossingDiff: Mapping: optional. Bossing: optional buff before the maintenance loop.

skills.role: Variant-dependent root/control that can simplify targeting.
whyUse: Community discussion treats it as a quality-of-life alternative that removes the need to aim ED precisely. Not a damage competitor.
whenReplace: Variant choice; some players prefer it over strict two-step targeting.
mappingBossingDiff: Mapping: optional control. Bossing: generally not part of the boss loop.
notes: Role as alternative pending PC verification.

skills.role: Variant-dependent AoE used for dense packs or as a boss tool in some guides.
whyUse: Some guides use it for extra pressure on dense packs or as a single-target option. Verify against your selected variant.
whenReplace: Variant choice; not core to the ED + Contagion loop.
mappingBossingDiff: Mapping: optional on dense packs. Bossing: optional in some single-target variants.

sections.title: Mapping
paragraphs: Cast Contagion into the center of a connected pack, then land Essence Drain on a target inside it — the ED debuff spreads to every nearby Contagion-affected enemy. Move immediately and watch whether the debuff propagates before spending another cast. Dark Effigy can be planted to auto-maintain ED/Despair on the cluster.
Tag a dense pack, confirm the spread starts, then move ahead. If propagation fails, check skill order (Contagion must be first), range, duration and whether the first target died with both effects.
bullets: Contagion → Essence Drain → move; optional Dark Effigy.
Fix cast order before blaming gear.
Reactive weapon upgrade when clear speed drops.

sections.title: Bossing
paragraphs: Open the boss fight in this order: Despair first (the curse, -chaos resistance), then Dark Effigy (plant the totem so it auto-applies ED + Despair), then Essence Drain to lay the main DoT. Contagion is normally skipped on a lone boss because there is nothing to spread to.

Sustain with a loop: re-apply Essence Drain before it expires, keep the Dark Effigy totem alive and repositioned (it can miss a moving boss, so you must re-cast ED yourself), refresh Despair when it falls off, and keep moving between mechanics. The rhythm is refresh → reposition → refresh, not stationary casting.
bullets: Open: Despair → Dark Effigy → Essence Drain.
Sustain: refresh ED → keep Effigy → refresh Despair → move.
No Contagion needed on a single boss.

items.question: Why does one pack disappear and the next barely moves?
answer: The successful pack likely received Contagion and Essence Drain on the same connected group. In the failed pack, ED may have hit outside the Contagion set or the monsters were too separated to propagate.
bullets: Aim Contagion at the pack center.
Wait long enough to observe the first spread.
Use terrain to group monsters before recasting.

items.question: Should I use Entangle instead?
answer: Use it if you value simpler targeting. Community discussion treats it as a quality-of-life alternative, not proof that ED + Contagion is invalid. The trade is a different clear pattern and support package.

items.question: What if I want a more immediate caster?
answer: The cold Chronomancer route has a more direct hit-and-freeze rhythm, but requires a staged gem swap and closer positioning.
